subject: Physics
q: A short electric dipole has dipole moment 16 × 10⁻⁹ C m. Find its electric potential at a point 0.6 m from its centre on a line making 60° with the dipole axis. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
hint: Use V = kp cos θ/r² for a short dipole.

subject: Physics
q: A capillary tube of radius r raises 5 g of water. What mass of water will rise in another capillary tube of radius 2r under the same conditions?
hint: Capillary rise h is inversely proportional to radius, while raised mass is proportional to r²h.
solution: m = ρπr²h and h ∝ 1/r, hence m ∝ r. Doubling the radius doubles the mass from 5 g to 10 g.

subject: Physics
q: What is the ratio of the contributions made by the electric-field and magnetic-field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave?
hint: In a plane electromagnetic wave, the time-averaged electric and magnetic energy densities are equal.
solution: The electric and magnetic fields make equal contributions to the wave energy and intensity, so the ratio is 1 : 1.

subject: Physics
q: A long solenoid 50 cm long has 100 turns and carries 2.5 A. What is the magnetic field at its centre? Take μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹.
hint: For a long solenoid, B = μ₀NI/L.

subject: Physics
q: For which species is the Bohr model not valid?
hint: The Bohr model applies to one-electron species.
solution: Hydrogen, deuterium and He⁺ each have one electron. Ne⁺ has nine electrons, so the one-electron Bohr model is not valid for it.

subject: Physics
q: What is the energy equivalent of 0.5 g of matter?
hint: Use E = mc² and convert grams to kilograms.

subject: Physics
q: Taking significant figures into account, what is 9.99 m − 0.0099 m?
hint: For subtraction, retain the least number of decimal places among the measurements.
solution: The exact difference is 9.9801 m. Since 9.99 m is given to two decimal places, the result rounds to 9.98 m.

subject: Physics
q: Two guitar strings A and B produce 6 beats per second. When the tension in B is slightly decreased, the beat frequency rises to 7 Hz. If A has frequency 530 Hz, what was the original frequency of B?
hint: Lowering B's tension lowers its frequency; use the direction in which the beat frequency changes.
solution: Originally B could be 536 or 524 Hz. Lowering B's frequency would reduce the beat rate if B were 536 Hz, but it increases the rate when B is below A. Therefore B was 530 − 6 = 524 Hz.

subject: Physics
q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an AC source. Removing L gives a phase difference π/3; removing C also gives a phase difference π/3. What is the power factor of the complete LCR circuit?
hint: The two reduced circuits give equal magnitudes of capacitive and inductive reactance relative to R.
solution: For RC, tanφ = X_C/R = √3. For RL, tanφ = X_L/R = √3. Thus X_L = X_C in the complete circuit, so it is at resonance and cosφ = 1.

subject: Physics
q: Two solid copper spheres have radii r₁ and r₂, where r₁ = 1.5r₂. What is the ratio of heat needed to raise their temperatures by 1 K?
hint: For the same material and temperature rise, heat is proportional to mass and hence volume.

subject: Physics
q: For an interface with an ordinary transparent medium, in which range should Brewster's angle iᵦ lie?
hint: Use tan iᵦ = n₂/n₁ for light entering a denser transparent medium.
solution: For air to an ordinary denser medium, n₂/n₁ > 1, so tan iᵦ > 1 and therefore 45° < iᵦ < 90°.

subject: Physics
q: Two equal-capacity cylinders are connected by a stopcock. One contains an ideal gas at STP and the other is evacuated. The system is thermally insulated and the stopcock is suddenly opened. How is the process classified?
hint: The combined system is thermally insulated during free expansion.
solution: No heat crosses the insulated boundary, so Q = 0. The free expansion is therefore adiabatic (and for an ideal gas its temperature also remains unchanged).

subject: Physics
q: An iron rod has magnetic susceptibility 599. What is its permeability? Take μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹.

subject: Physics
q: A parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance 6 μF with air and 30 μF after a dielectric is inserted. What is the permittivity of the dielectric? Take ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻².
hint: The dielectric constant equals the capacitance ratio.

subject: Physics
q: A charged particle has drift velocity 7.5 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ in an electric field of 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ V m⁻¹. What is its mobility in m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹?
hint: Mobility is drift speed divided by electric-field magnitude.
